title: Can You Use a Cycling Helmet for Skating?
thumbnail_text: Can your bike helmet keep you safe skating?

scenes.heading: Can You Use a Cycling Helmet for Skating?
scenes.sub: What EN1078 covers, and where a bike helmet falls short
scenes.narration: Can you wear your cycling helmet for skating? By the end of this guide, you will know when a bike helmet is enough, and when to buy a skating helmet instead. This is one of the most common questions we get. Usually it comes from a parent who already owns a bike helmet. The short answer is this. A certified cycling helmet is almost always better than no helmet. And in Europe, the same standard covers both sports. But there are real differences. One of them matters a lot for beginners.

scenes.heading: One standard, three activities
bullets: EN1078 is the European helmet standard
It covers cyclists
It covers skateboarders and roller skaters
A CE EN1078 mark means tested for skating
scenes.narration: Start with the certification. EN1078 is the European standard for helmets. Its scope is clear. It covers helmets for cyclists, and for users of skateboards and roller skates. One standard, three activities. So a helmet with a CE EN1078 mark has been tested for skating use. That is true whether the box shows a bicycle or a skateboard.

scenes.heading: The real question to ask
bullets: Has this helmet been tested at all?
Many cheap skating helmets list no certification
A certified bike helmet beats an uncertified skate helmet
scenes.narration: This is the part most people miss. The question is not really bike helmet or skate helmet. The question is whether the helmet in your hands has been tested to any standard at all. A great many cheap helmets sold for skating carry no stated certification. So an EN1078 cycling helmet from a reputable brand is the better choice. It beats an uncertified helmet that is simply sold as a skating helmet.

scenes.heading: Coverage at the back of the head
bullets: Road helmets sit higher at the back
Skate helmets come lower over the skull
Beginners fall backwards
Rear coverage matters most for learners
scenes.narration: Now, where does a cycling helmet fall short? There are three practical differences. The first is the important one. Coverage at the back of the head. Road cycling helmets are shaped around the risk of going over the bars. So they extend forward and sit higher at the back. Skate style helmets come further down over the back of the skull. Here is why that matters. Beginner skaters fall backwards. Your feet slide out in front of you. The back of your head is the first thing to reach the ground. That is exactly the area a road helmet covers least. If you are learning, or buying for a child who is learning, that extra rear coverage is not a detail.

scenes.heading: One big impact, then replace it
bullets: Most EN1078 helmets use EPS foam
The foam crushes once and does not recover
ASTM F1492 tests for multiple impacts
Replace any helmet after a big impact
scenes.narration: The second difference is repeated impacts. Most EN1078 helmets, cycling and skating alike, use EPS foam. That foam crushes once to absorb energy, and it does not recover. So they are single impact helmets. Some skate style helmets are built to a different standard, such as the American ASTM F1492. It tests for multiple impacts. That is useful if you are learning tricks and going down again and again. Either way, follow one rule. Replace any helmet after a significant impact, even if the shell looks perfect. The damage is in the liner, and you cannot see it.

scenes.heading: Ventilation, weight and shape
bullets: Road helmets are light and well vented
Hard shell skate helmets run hot
A hot helmet stays in the bag
scenes.narration: The third difference is ventilation, weight and shape. Road cycling helmets are usually well ventilated and light. That is why they transfer well to skating. Classic skate style helmets have a hard shell and few vents. They are hot. And in Indian conditions, a hot helmet is a helmet that stays in the bag. The best helmet is the one you actually wear.

scenes.heading: What about speed skating?
bullets: Inline speed needs light and well vented
The needs look more like cycling
Short track ice needs its own helmet
scenes.narration: What about speed skating? For inline speed and road skating, a light, well ventilated helmet is the right tool. The needs look much more like cycling than skateboarding. You move fast in a straight line. You want airflow. And you want the lowest weight on your neck over a long session. That is why LiveLica skating helmets are shaped more like a road cycling helmet than a skate park helmet. Short track ice racing is the exception. Those helmets are a compact, low profile shell, made to sit under a race hood. They are designed with close pack racing in mind. A cycling helmet is not a substitute there.

scenes.heading: Which skater are you?
bullets: Learner or child: buy rear coverage
Recreational with a certified bike helmet: wear it
Inline speed: light, vented, certified
Short track ice: buy the short track helmet
scenes.chapter: Should you buy a skating helmet?
scenes.narration: So should you buy a skating helmet? Be honest about which skater you are. If you are learning to skate, or buying for a child, get a skate style helmet with proper rear coverage. Backward falls are the whole reason. If you skate for fun and already own a certified cycling helmet, wear it. It is tested to the right standard, and it is on your head. That is most of the battle. For inline speed or road skating, put weight, ventilation and a certified shell first. A good road cycling helmet works. A purpose built skating helmet does the same job, with a fit made for your skating position. And for short track ice, buy the short track helmet.

scenes.heading: How any helmet should fit
bullets: Measure 2 cm above your eyebrows
Sit level, two fingers above the brows
No shifting before you tighten
Two fingers under the chin strap
scenes.narration: Whatever you choose, fit matters. A helmet that fits badly does only a fraction of its job. Measure around your head, about two centimetres above your eyebrows. Buy to that number. The helmet should sit level, about two finger widths above your eyebrows. It should feel snug, with no pressure points. Shake your head before you tighten anything. The helmet should not shift. Then set the chin strap so two fingers fit between the strap and your chin.

scenes.heading: For a beginner, buy for the backward fall
scenes.sub: Full guide at livelica.com, link in the description
scenes.narration: Here is the summary. A certified cycling helmet is a real skating helmet. The standard says so. It is weaker at the back of the head, and that matters most for the people who fall the most. If you already own one, wear it today. If you are buying for a beginner, buy for the backward fall. The full guide is on the LiveLica blog, and the link is in the description.
